This integration connects Gladys to **your Vogel's MotionMount motorized TV
mount** (Signature, TVM 7675 Pro) over its **local protocol** (TCP, port 23, on
the Ethernet cable of the mount). The MotionMount becomes a device in the
**Discovery** tab of Gladys: position, motion, errors, a list to go to a preset
and a **Stop** button. Everything stays on your local network. Unofficial, not
affiliated with Vogel's.

> **Development version (0.1).** Written from the python-MotionMount library
> published by Vogel's, and tested against a simulated MotionMount only: it has
> **never been tested with a real MotionMount** yet. Feedback is welcome on the
> GitHub repository.

## Safety first

A motorized mount can **pinch** a hand between the TV and the wall, or **hit**
a person, a piece of furniture or an object. That is why:

- **moves are off by default**: tick "Allow moves" first;
- a move goes through a **list** ("Go to a preset"), never a switch: a "turn
  everything off" scene or voice assistant does not trigger it;
- a preset beyond the **bounds** you choose (extension, turn) is refused;
- a move is refused while the mount reports an **obstruction**, a motor error,
  an internal error or a TV width error;
- the **Stop** button does not depend on the moves option.

The protections of the mount itself (obstruction detection) come first: only
automate a move when nobody can stand in its way.

## What you get

| Feature        | In Gladys                                                         |
| -------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Extension (%)  | 0 = against the wall, 100 = arm fully out (read only)             |
| Turn (%)       | -100 to 100 (read only)                                           |
| Moving         | the motors run (read only)                                        |
| Status         | "OK" or the errors the mount reports (read only)                  |
| Go to a preset | the wall, or a preset 1 to 7 set on the mount; **off by default** |
| Stop           | stops the mount where it is                                       |

Positions are those of the mount (percent of its travel), not centimetres nor
degrees. Presets are set in the Vogel's app; the list follows their names at
each read.

## Requirements

- A MotionMount Signature (TVM 7675 Pro) wired with an **Ethernet cable** to
  the network of Gladys (the RS-232 link is not supported).
- Its IP address, preferably fixed (reserved in your router). Names in
  `.local` do not resolve in the integration container.
- If a **PIN of the User level** is set on the mount: that PIN.
- A firmware that gives the MAC address of the mount (`mac`): it is the
  identity of the device in Gladys. An older mount without it is not added (the
  status says so).

## Setup

1. In Gladys, open the **Vogel's MotionMount** integration, **Configuration**
   tab.
2. Type the **address** of the MotionMount, like `192.168.1.50` (or
   `192.168.1.50:2323` for another port).
3. Only when the mount has a PIN: type it in **PIN**. It is kept by Gladys in
   its database, never shown again; it is sent only to the MotionMount, and only
   when the mount asks for it, once per connection.
4. Save, then click **Test the connection**: the state of the mount shows.
5. Open the **Discovery** tab and add the MotionMount.
6. To control the moves, tick **Allow moves** and set the bounds.

## Options

- **Allow moves** (off by default): "Go to a preset" moves the TV.
- **Maximum extension** (100 % by default) and **Maximum turn** (100 % by
  default, each side): a preset beyond them is refused. The wall (extension 0,
  turn 0) is always within them.
- **Read interval** (60 s by default, 30 to 600 s): how often the state is read
  again. The mount also tells its changes on the connection, which stays open.
  After a command, the state is read at 2, 8, 20 and 45 s.
- **Language of the feature names**.

## How the commands are handled

**Go to a preset**: right before acting, the integration reads the errors of
the mount and the preset asked (set? within the bounds?), then sends the
command. One move at a time: the next one waits until the previous one is
sent. The command is refused, **nothing sent**, when:

- the value is not a preset from 0 to 7, or no address is configured;
- the moves option is off (checked on arrival, after the reads and right
  before sending);
- the mount is not connected (or its first read is not finished), or its
  identity (MAC address) is not the one of the device;
- the mount asks for a PIN that is missing, refused, or asks to wait after
  failed attempts, or the connection was cut twice in a row right after the
  PIN was sent;
- the previous move left without confirmation less than 30 s ago and the
  mount has not reached it yet;
- the mount could not be read before acting (no answer, connection lost,
  value not readable);
- the preset is not set, or is beyond the bounds;
- the mount reports an error (obstruction, motor, internal, width);
- a stop arrived meanwhile, or the configuration changed meanwhile;
- the connection was lost before sending, or the command could not leave
  within 3.5 s.

Once the command is written:

- the mount may **refuse** it itself (`#4xx`): nothing is done, the refusal is
  reported;
- without an answer of the mount, it is reported "sent, without
  confirmation", and never sent again by itself.

**Stop**: the MotionMount protocol has no stop command. The integration reads
the current position and sends it back as the new target: the motors stop
where they are. A position read up to 5 points outside the travel (mechanical
play) is brought back to the bound; further, nothing is written.

- The stop does not depend on the moves option and cancels the moves not sent
  yet.
- It goes before the other requests not sent yet, and waits 1 s at most for
  the request on the wire, a previous stop included (then the connection is
  cut and opened again).
- Each read of the stop waits 1.5 s at most; when a read fails before sending
  (a stale or cut connection), a new connection is opened and the stop tried
  once more, within the deadline.
- When the mount is not connected, the stop opens a connection at once, even
  during the wait after a failure.
- Several presses while a stop is not sent yet share that stop.
- While the container starts, the stop waits for the configuration (2 s at
  most).
- When a PIN is typed and the mount asks for it, the stop sends it; a PIN the
  mount refused is not sent again, but one held because of two cuts is (once
  per press).

1.5 s after a stop (answered, or sent without an answer), the integration reads
the motion of the mount (opening a connection when needed). When it still
moves, or cannot tell, the stop is sent again, and so on, 3 times at most; a
re-send that fails does not end these rounds. They end when a move was sent
after the stop, or when the configuration changes. They are not kept in
`/data`: a restart of the container in the seconds after the stop loses them.

The cases where the stop fails:

- no address is configured (after the wait of the start);
- the mount does not answer: no connection, or reads without an answer on the
  first connection and then on the new one;
- the current position cannot be read, or is not understood (too far outside
  the travel): nothing is written;
- the mount refuses the stop or a read (`#401`: PIN missing, refused or a wait
  imposed; `#400`, `#403`, `#405`...);
- the stop could not leave within 3.5 s;
- it is written without an answer: "sent, without confirmation" (then checked
  as above);
- it went to another MotionMount than the one of the device (another MAC
  address answers at the address): sent, but reported, since the mount of the
  device may not be stopped.

## Privacy and security

- The PIN is written neither to the logs, nor to the connection status, nor to
  `/data`. An address the integration does not understand is not shown back
  either (only its length): a PIN pasted in the wrong field does not show.
- When the mount refuses the PIN (or the connection is cut twice in a row
  right after it), only an **8-bit mark** (a truncated salted hash, shared by
  about 39 PINs out of 9999) is kept in `/data`, to see that the PIN typed
  changed. The PIN is not sent again by itself until another PIN or a click on
  **Test the connection** (one try); only the stop still sends it, once per
  press, when the hold comes from cuts.
- The MotionMount protocol travels in clear on your local network.
- No cloud, no account, no Bluetooth.

## Troubleshooting

- **Unreachable**: check the IP address and the Ethernet cable; the mount
  answers on port 23. After a failure, the integration tries again after 30 s,
  1, 2 then 5 min, and at least the interval (the **Test the connection**
  button too, restarts included: the time of the last attempt is kept in
  `/data`). Exceptions: a stop and its checks, and the reads that follow a
  command, may open a connection sooner.
- **Identity cannot be read**: firmware too old (no MAC address); update the
  mount with the Vogel's app.
- **Preset not reached** (orange dot): an obstruction, a hand on the TV or a
  stop interrupted the travel.

## Konfigurationseinstellungen

Diese Einstellungen fragt Vogel's MotionMount in seinem Konfigurationsbildschirm in Gladys ab.

| Einstellung | Typ | Pflichtfeld | Beschreibung |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Your MotionMount in Gladys | `section` | Nein | The MotionMount (Signature, TVM 7675 Pro) becomes a device in the Discovery tab: extension, turn, motion, errors, a list to go to a preset and a Stop button. Everything stays on your local network (TCP port 23, Ethernet). Moves are off by default: a motorized mount can pinch or hit. Never tested with a real MotionMount yet. Unofficial, not affiliated with Vogel's. |
| Address of the MotionMount | `string` | Ja | Its local IP address (port 23 by default, or address:port). Give it a fixed address in your router (DHCP reservation). One MotionMount per integration. |
| PIN (optional) | `secret` | Nein | Only if a PIN of the User level is set on the mount (a number from 1 to 9999). Kept by Gladys in its database, never shown again; sent only to the MotionMount, and only when it asks for it. |
| Allow moves | `boolean` | Nein | Off by default. On, "Go to a preset" moves the TV (the wall or a preset set on the mount), from Gladys, scenes or voice assistants. Make sure nobody and nothing stands in its way. Stop does not depend on this option. |
| Maximum extension (%) | `number` | Nein | A preset whose extension goes beyond it is refused (0 to 100 %, 100 = the full arm). |
| Maximum turn (%) | `number` | Nein | A preset turned further, on either side, is refused (0 to 100 %). |
| Read interval (s) | `number` | Nein | How often the state is read again (30 to 600 s); the mount also tells its changes as they come. After a failure, the next connection waits at least this long. |
| Language of the feature names | `select` | Nein | Used for the names of the features and presets of the mount added from now on. |

## So installierst du Vogel's MotionMount in Gladys

1. Öffne in Gladys **Integrationen**: Vogel's MotionMount erscheint im Katalog neben den nativen Integrationen, mit einem Community-Badge.
2. Klicke auf **Installieren**. Gladys lädt das Docker-Image (`ghcr.io/lm1lc3n7/gladys-motionmount:0.1.1`) herunter, startet es in einer vom Kern isolierten Sandbox und erzeugt die Oberfläche der Integration (Geräte, Erkennung und Konfiguration).
3. Öffne den Bildschirm **Konfiguration** der Integration, fülle die Einstellungen aus und speichere.
4. Du kannst sie auch direkt über die URL ihres Repositorys installieren: [https://github.com/LM1LC3N7/gladys-motionmount](https://github.com/LM1LC3N7/gladys-motionmount).

Vogel's MotionMount benötigt Gladys `>=5.1.0`. Der Katalog in Gladys wird stündlich aktualisiert, eine neue Version ist also spätestens eine Stunde nach ihrer Veröffentlichung verfügbar.

Du nutzt Gladys noch nicht? Es ist kostenlos und Open Source: [folge der Installationsanleitung](/de/docs/), um loszulegen.

## Über externe Integrationen

Vogel's MotionMount ist eine **externe Integration**: eine Community-Integration, die als Docker-Container verpackt und auf GitHub veröffentlicht wird. Gladys installiert sie mit einem Klick und führt sie in einer vom Kern isolierten Sandbox aus. Sie wird von [LM1LC3N7](https://github.com/LM1LC3N7) veröffentlicht und gepflegt, nicht vom Gladys-Kernteam.
